findings.section: D1 - one GEFSv12 bias map on reforecast + operational overlap (amendment section 2c)
findings.issue: Labelled an interpretation, but it changes 'for each product': one GEFSv12 map is fitted on reforecast plus operational overlap, and the code also merges P2 and P3 into one product slot. The reading is defensible, identical for every NWP-using arm, and only weather enters. Not in the entry: the fit mask is on issue dates, so in CV processes gridMET weather of lead days up to 2021-10-07 (val block) enters the map; the pooled fallback is fitted over all loaded sites (train+val roles) with as few as 3 points; there are two extra fallback tiers and a slope clip; the map is dominated by reforecast years while every val-block issue is operational.
findings.evidence: (a) Stamped 2c: 'For each product and lead day, a per-site linear map from forecast to gridMET is fitted on train-block overlap only: GEFS reforecast: WY2008–2021-09-30 ∩ product availability; GFS: 2021-03-24..2021-09-30.' Reforecast ends 2019-12-31, so the stamped window only makes sense with P3 included, and no separate P3 window is stamped. Literal alternative: a P3-only map (about 1 year, under 60 days per month, so pooled HUC2 by the stamped rule). (b) The same bias-corrected tensors feed SONDE-HF, R-NH, GBM-NWP, PF-GBM and Chronos-2-cov: parity kept; an operational-vs-reforecast bias would hit all alike. (c) No sonde target. /home/bcheng/STOCKHOLM/SENTINEL-STOCKHOLM/sentinel/models/sonde_v2/products.py line 56 train_mask = dates <= TRAIN_END (issue dates); /home/bcheng/STOCKHOLM/SENTINEL-STOCKHOLM/sentinel/models/sonde_v2/nwp.py fit_bias_map lines 128-167 pairs lead days 1-7, so 7 val-block weather days enter when the cube runs past 2021-09-30 (CV) but not in step 1: the map differs between step 1 and CV. (d) products.py lines 52-58 implement the merge (line 54 np.where(isfinite(reforecast), reforecast, operational)); GFS own map lines 66-67. nwp.py _fit_lin needs only 3 points and clips the slope to [0.5, 1.5] (line 124); tiers are site-month (>= 60) -> pooled group-month -> site-all-months (>= 60) -> identity, although the entry says 'pooled HUC2 fallback is unchanged'. Untested on data: no operational extraction exists yet (see U4).
findings.suggested_ruling: Approve with conditions: (1) the merged GEFSv12 map is final and is not changed after any validation number; (2) only forecast-observation pairs whose valid day is <= 2021-09-30 enter any bias map, in step 1 and CV alike; (3) the tier order, the 3-point minimum and the slope clip [0.5, 1.5] are recorded as part of D1; (4) before the first validation number a weather-only train-block diagnostic (mean residual of bias-corrected P3 against gridMET, 2020-09-23..2021-09-30, per lead and field) is logged to the registry, report-only.

findings.section: D2 - GBM-type references fitted with 7 levels (Q) or location-scale (LS) instead of 19 quantile boosters (amendment section 2b)
findings.issue: Not an interpretation. 'Quantile LightGBM (19 levels)' is replaced by 7 fitted levels interpolated to 19 (Q) or by an L1 location plus a scale model with pooled residual quantiles (LS, which is not quantile LightGBM). 12 of the 19 scored levels of GBM-NWP, PF-GBM and therefore E2-B are not trained, while the candidate has a native 19-level head. The 'no gain' claim has no evidence in the repo. The step-1 gate uses the 7-level default as its comparator. The file is out of step with the code, which already carries the literal Q19 configuration.

findings.suggested_ruling: Reject as written. The author must rewrite D2 as a deviation in which: Q19 (19 fitted levels) is a mandatory configuration of GBM-NWP and of PF-GBM and is the 'default config' of the step-1 contrast; Q and LS are additional configurations inside the limit of 5; each reference's reported configuration (also inside E2-B) is the one chosen by the section 2h within-family criterion; the configuration lists are written to the parity log, hashed and registry-logged before the first reference run; the 'no gain' sentence is removed or backed by train-block-only evidence. findings.issue: A limited exception to the stamped 'no zero-fill', not a pure interpretation. Product-level masking is kept and the batch code is the same for SONDE-HF and R-NH, so parity holds and no protected value enters. But the entry's purpose (use GFS temperature before 2024-01-20) is not delivered in the CV code: the GFS slot is never available to either network (U1). The code zero-fills any missing field, not only precipitation and shortwave.
findings.evidence: (a) Stamped 2c: 'combined in SONDE-HF / R-NH by a masked mean over the available products, with no zero-fill'. (b) /home/bcheng/STOCKHOLM/SENTINEL-STOCKHOLM/sentinel/models/sonde_v2/data_v2.py lines 120-128: one code path for both networks; GBM-type models and Chronos-2-cov get NaN natively. The fill value 0 is the train-block mean in standardised units (statistics from rows <= 2021-09-30, weather only, lines 84-89). (c) None. findings.section: D5 - stage 2 and GBM-type references use real GEFS where it exists, perfect-prog plus error model in the GEFSv11 gap (amendment section 2c)
findings.issue: A change of two stamped sentences, with an inaccurate reason, and the code is broader than the entry. The stamped gap rule already keeps gap rows (other products, else past-weather mode), and GBM-type fit rows end 2019-09-30, so they never reach the gap. In the code the perfect-prog fill is element-wise wherever GEFS is missing on any train-block date, and the LS residual slice and all early-stopping rows use these filled inputs although the configuration comment says calibration uses issued forecasts.
findings.evidence: (a) Stamped 2c: 'Stage 2 fine-tunes on real reforecasts over the train block. Validation, selection, calibration and ensemble weights use archived issued forecasts only (M1-N C-N2), for every model alike.' and 'Issues whose lead days fall in that gap use the other available products, else past-weather mode, and are reported as such.' (b) Same rule for SONDE-HF, R-NH, GBM-NWP and PF-GBM; Chronos-2-cov is zero-shot. Parity kept. But the LS reference's residual quantiles are computed partly on perfect-prog inputs (about 266 of about 688 calibration issue days lie in 2020-01-01..2020-09-22) and are then applied to issued forecasts, which can mis-size that reference's intervals. (c) No val or test value: /home/bcheng/STOCKHOLM/SENTINEL-STOCKHOLM/scripts/train/sonde_v2_cv.py line 120 restores real GEFS outside the train block; early-stopping rows are train-block (line 230). (d) cv.py line 119 g_real = np.where(np.isfinite(prod.gefs), prod.gefs, prod.pp): the fill is per element, on any date and for any cause (missing file, failed extraction), not only the gap, and no count is logged ('reported as such' is not met). Line 238 passes nwp_eval=comb_train, so /home/bcheng/STOCKHOLM/SENTINEL-STOCKHOLM/sentinel/models/sonde_v2/gbm_nwp.py line 173 (calibration table; line 46 cal_on_eval 'archived issued forecasts (C-N2)') and GBM early stopping use the filled tensor; stage-2 early stopping does the same (train_v2.py evaluate_loss). /home/bcheng/STOCKHOLM/SENTINEL-STOCKHOLM/sentinel/models/sonde/gbm.py lines 49 and 63: fit rows have target <= 2019-09-30, so 'would remove 9 months of training rows from every model' is false for GBM-type models.
findings.suggested_ruling: Approve with conditions: perfect-prog substitution applies only to whole GEFS product-leads of issue dates 2020-01-01..2020-09-22; any other missing GEFS value stays missing (masked or NaN); the LS residual slice and the early-stopping rows of stage 2 and of GBM-type models exclude substituted rows; each run logs its count of substituted rows; the reason given in the entry is corrected in the rulings file.
